metadata.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Double Q-learning (van Hasselt, Guez, Silver, 2015)
metadata.framework: Double DQN: decoupling action selection from value estimation in deep Q-learning to reduce overestimation bias
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on arXiv:1509.06461 PDF text.

nodes.name: Q-learning overestimation
nodes.statement: Standard Q-learning uses $\max_a Q(s', a)$ as the target value, which uses the same values both to select and evaluate an action. Because $\mathbb{E}[\max_a Q(s', a)] \geq \max_a \mathbb{E}[Q(s', a)]$ (Jensen's inequality), this systematically overestimates action values when estimation errors are present.

nodes.name: Double Q-learning principle
nodes.statement: Use two value functions to decouple action selection from action evaluation. One set of weights $\theta$ selects the greedy action: $a^* = \arg\max_a Q(s', a; \theta)$, and a second set of weights $\theta'$ evaluates that action: $Q(s', a^*; \theta')$. The Double Q-learning target is $Y^{\mathrm{Double}} = r + \gamma Q(s', \arg\max_a Q(s', a; \theta); \theta')$.

nodes.name: Double DQN
nodes.statement: Apply the Double Q-learning idea to DQN by using the online network weights $\theta$ for action selection and the target network weights $\theta^-$ for action evaluation. The Double DQN target is: $Y^{\mathrm{DoubleDQN}}_t = r_{t+1} + \gamma Q(s_{t+1}, \arg\max_a Q(s_{t+1}, a; \theta_t); \theta^-_t)$. This requires no additional networks or parameters beyond what DQN already maintains.

nodes.name: Double Q-learning is unbiased under conditions
nodes.statement: If the two sets of weights $\theta$ and $\theta'$ are updated on disjoint sets of experiences (as in the original Double Q-learning of van Hasselt 2010), the resulting estimator is unbiased. Even when the same experiences are used (as in Double DQN), the estimator has lower bias than the standard max estimator.

nodes.name: DQN overestimation is substantial in practice
nodes.statement: Experiments on Atari 2600 games show that DQN significantly overestimates action values in many games. The overestimation grows with training and correlates with poor policy quality. Double DQN produces much more accurate value estimates.

nodes.name: Performance improvement over DQN
nodes.statement: Double DQN improves upon DQN on most of the 49 Atari games tested, with the median normalized human-start score increasing from 68% (DQN) to 116% (Double DQN). The improvement is especially large on games where DQN overestimates most.
